description.narrative: (Mauritania): USAID Nafoore (which means "added value" in Pulaar) aims to increase the ability of vulnerable Mauritanian youth to resist radicalization and recruitment by violent extremism organizations (VEO) in the four regions of Nouakchott, Trarza, Hodh El Gharbi and Hodh El Chargui. Grounded in Positive Youth Development (PYD), the activity works closely with youth-serving organizations (YSOs) to reinforce the shared social values of Mauritanian youth that are incongruent with violent extremism and to create opportunities for giving youth a sense of belonging. Additionally, USAID Nafoore focuses on equipping vulnerable youth with the skills and vocational training needed to find employment, addressing the social and economic drivers that lead to youth participation in violent extremism..USAID Nafoore plans to use FY 2024 funding to scale up work on two fronts. First, in response to the needs identified by the assessments for "social connection and belonging," Nafoore will strengthen networks and hubs of youth-led, youth-serving organizations that offer young people in the four target regions ways to connect with other youth that share their values. The activity will also create opportunities to demonstrate leadership, community service, and other positive ways that young people can influence and shape their communities. Second, in response to the need to address economic drivers, with FY 2024 funding, Nafoore will provide opportunities for an estimated 400 more youth in Hodh el Chargi, Hodh el Gharbi and Traza regions to learn soft skills and receive vocational training in areas identified by the Labor Market Assessment, namely in the information technology, tourism, agriculture, and fisheries sectors. ..
